clue.text: One finds reason for passing nothing during recess

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a corner is a nook or recess
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone explaining a death keeps finding nothing during a parliamentary recess.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside COR-NER to make CORONER. 'Passing' here means dying, not walking by.
explanation.definitionFit: An official holds inquests to establish the cause of an unexpected death.

clue.text: Sign over hotel is a dubious one

indicators.note: the sign is placed over the hotel, covering it, so it encloses the next letter

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The sign above a hotel looks shady.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside CANCER after its first letter: C-H-ANCER. 'One' refers back to the hotel sign in the surface but means a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a chancer is an opportunist who takes risks and may be untrustworthy.

clue.text: Rebuke socialist changing positions where celebrities are found

indicators.note: the two pieces swap places, so they are joined in the opposite order to the clue

parts.note: red is the colour of socialism
to carpet someone is British slang for reprimanding them

explanation.surface: A left-winger is told off for switching his political stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives CARPET then RED; swapping them gives RED CARPET.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars arrive at premieres and awards ceremonies walking along a long crimson rug.

clue.text: Feed is fetched using this step

definitions.note: a playful clue to the letters that turn one word into another
definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsical: cut T, C and H into feed, as if adding ..., and you get fetched
second meaning: a level or degree on a scale

explanation.walkthrough: FEED becomes FETCHED when TCH is inserted, and NO-TCH is a playful way to point at those letters; the clean definition is 'step'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving up a notch means going one level higher, so the word is a degree or grade.

clue.text: Keep progressing area extended under foundation

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means coming after, so these pieces follow

parts.note: rock is a solid foundation
A is an abbreviation for area
long means extended

explanation.surface: Building work carries on as the site is widened beneath its base.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock along is an informal phrase for carrying on steadily, getting by without trouble.

clue.text: Girl getting introduced by lecturer during professional disaster

indicators.note: the first word is introduced, placed at the front, ahead of what follows

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society girl

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so lecturer goes inside professional

parts.note: an ace is an expert
L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A young woman is introduced to her tutor in the middle of a work catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' and 'professional' read as people in a story; DEB is the crossword stock word for a young society woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden complete failure or fiasco, a synonym for a calamity.

clue.text: Horror is not quite real when shown in 2-D

indicators.note: shown in means placed inside, so the shortened word sits between the outer letters
falling just short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the first of two Ds
taken as written
the second of two Ds

explanation.surface: A horror film seems less real when shown flat rather than in 3-D.
explanation.walkthrough: 2-D is read as two Ds; REAL loses its L and sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or terror, a close synonym for alarm and fright.

clue.text: Didn't pursue report of second reservation

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to back is to second a proposal, and a doubt is a reservation

explanation.surface: News of a second room booking.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from a commitment or plan rather than continuing with it.

clue.text: Property of double bluff

wordplay.note: two words for a bluff or trick: con and do, as in 'do someone out of money'

explanation.surface: A piece of real estate is used in a double bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' asks for two synonyms of bluff side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for condominium, an apartment owned individually within a shared building; real estate.

clue.text: Controversial reason for electronic crime, perhaps

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a motive is the reason for a crime, the 'perhaps' showing crime is only one example

explanation.surface: A disputed explanation of a computer offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'reason for crime, perhaps' around the inserted 'electronic', which supplies the leading E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feeling, so it tends to be hotly debated.

clue.text: Inspect valued gift on a regular basis

indicators.note: regular intervals mean every other letter is taken from the words given

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone checks a precious present at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit is to examine accounts or procedures officially and closely.

clue.text: Endless street party that's getting louder

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of street is cut off

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street of houses
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A never-ending street party grows ever noisier.
explanation.walkthrough: CRESCENT loses its last letter to make CRESCEN, then DO is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term marking a gradual increase in volume, used for anything building in intensity.

clue.text: Family embracing headstrong daughter fail spectacularly

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so family wraps around the next word

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
rash means impetuous
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family hugging their wilful daughter ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The family wraps only around the headstrong part; the daughter tags on at the very end, outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash-land is literally to bring an aircraft down hard; figuratively it means to collapse in failure.

clue.text: During demo, jihadis display sign of feeling

indicators.note: the letters wanted occur during the run of words, sitting inside them

parts.note: found across the end of demo and the start of jihadis

explanation.surface: Protesters at a demonstration show what they feel.
explanation.definitionFit: These small pictograms in text messages express a mood or reaction, such as a smiley face.

clue.text: They're known to have experience making boxing rings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the idiom 'know the ____', to be experienced

definitions.note: the things that make up a boxing ring
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the cords that enclose a boxing ring

explanation.walkthrough: The first half rests on the phrase 'to know the ropes', meaning to be familiar with how things are done.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick cords are what experienced hands are said to know, and they also fence in a fighting square.

clue.text: Longest in bats for just one run

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so these letters go wild

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The longest-serving batsman goes in to score a mere single.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides an anagram; in cricket a single is one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a lone item; the cricket single, one run, is the example in view.

clue.text: Naturally embracing fellow that's lost

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so naturally wraps around the next word

parts.note: 'of course' means naturally, obviously
F is an abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone naturally hugs a man who has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside OF COURSE after OF, making OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off the planned route means having strayed from the right direction, i.e. astray.

clue.text: Comical cleric destined to take on the right

indicators.note: to take on is to take in or absorb, so destined holds the following words

parts.note: fated means destined
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A funny priest is fated to side with the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: FATHER TED is a 1990s British-made TV sitcom about a hapless Irish priest, which is why the cleric is comical.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a celebrated comedy series is a hapless priest on an Irish island.

clue.text: Come up again to put new top on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rise back to the surface, reappear
second meaning: lay a fresh surface, as on a road

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both reappearing after being submerged and laying fresh paving on a road.

clue.text: Gent had it prepared for special meal with his partner

indicators.note: to prepare something is to make it ready, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has everything ready for a romantic dinner with his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple's evening set aside for romance, commonly involving dinner out together.

clue.text: Bound to involve bribe when turning over bank …

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the result is read backwards
to involve is to include, so bound holds the next word inside it

parts.note: tied means bound
a sop is a small concession given to placate someone

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to bribe officials when turning over a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue for the surface but carries no wordplay; 'bank' is a verb here, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank money is to place it in an account for safe keeping.

clue.text: Sounds of disapproval about American actions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sounds go around the next word

parts.note: tsk is a clicking noise of disapproval
A is a common abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: People tut-tut over what an American has done.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits inside TSKS: T-A-SKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs or pieces of work to be done, so things done or deeds.

clue.text: … bonus almost certain before it's over

indicators.note: almost the whole word means its last letter is missing
coming before it means placed first, with the earlier piece following

parts.note: sure means certain
a plus is an added benefit or bonus

explanation.surface: A payment is almost certain to arrive before the job is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonus' looks like the definition but is wordplay, and 'it' points back to it; the definition is 'over', as in left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over is in excess of what is needed, an extra remaining amount.

clue.text: Part of a rose, say, that's favourite with nearly everyone

indicators.note: nearly the whole word means it falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A rose is everyone's favourite flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you a rose is just one example of a flower that has these parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Any flower, a rose included, has these coloured leaf-like parts of its corolla.

clue.text: Message is dry with little content

indicators.note: having content means holding something inside, so dry is filled with little

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. not drinking alcohol
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A dull message with hardly anything in it.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, for teetotal, is the crossword stock answer for dry; wee is Scots for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post on the social network formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: Officer who will cherish organisation's resources

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the official who looks after a body's funds
second meaning, playful: someone who will prize something, a verb for prize with a doer ending

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the answer as 'one who treasures', i.e. cherishes, the funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A society or club elects an official to manage its money and keep its accounts.

clue.text: Keying errors dame made from form, for example

parts.note: surface reading: a noblewoman crafted out of some form

parts.words: dame made from form, for example
parts.note: setter's reading: dame is made mistyped, and from is form mistyped, both slips of the keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: The examples are themselves the answer: 'dame' and 'from' are TYPOS for 'made' and 'form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakes made while pressing keys, such as transposed letters, are small printing slips.

clue.text: Run? Strangely, yes and no

parts.note: surface reading: an ambiguous answer to whether to run
setter's reading: the word means to run for office and also to stay still, the opposite of running

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain you STAND for election where Americans run; but to STAND is also to stay still, not running at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Contesting an election is called standing in Britain, equivalent to running for office elsewhere.

clue.text: Confectioner's outlet, the best place for making contact?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a spot where candy is sold

definitions.text: the best place for making contact
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ideal point on a bat or racket to strike a ball

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is whimsical, a candy outlet taken word by word; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: In bat and racket sports the term names the point giving maximum power with least effort.

clue.text: Benefit from circulating hot stuff around island

indicators.note: going round turns the hot stuff back to front
around means encircling, so the hot stuff wraps the island

parts.note: molten rock from a volcano
I is an abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island profits from volcanic heat flowing around it.
explanation.walkthrough: LAVA reversed is AVAL, which takes I inside: AVA-I-L.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of avail is to be of use, so the noun means advantage or use.

clue.text: Test missing section attached to waste outlet creating disease

indicators.note: section is S, and missing it means that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the body's exit for waste

explanation.surface: A test of the drains turns up a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the standard abbreviation for section, so only that one letter goes from the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, commonly called lockjaw.

clue.text: Freakishly odd stones are a fairground attraction

indicators.note: something freakish is strange and out of normal order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
gems are precious stones

explanation.surface: Bizarre rocks are on show at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at funfairs, small electric cars driven to bump into each other.
